record.paper_title: Quadratic Stochastic Operators: Results and Open Problems
record.original_question: Let V be a Volterra quadratic stochastic operator on S^{m-1}, and let tau be a permutation of {1, ..., m}. Define the permuted Volterra operator V_tau by permuting the output coordinates of V according to tau; when tau is not the identity this operator is non-Volterra. For arbitrary tau, determine the asymptotic behavior of trajectories of V_tau, including convergence, periodic behavior, omega-limit sets, and other possible long-term dynamics.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $S^{m-1} = \{x = (x_1, \ldots, x_m) \in \mathbb{R}^m : x_i \geq 0, \ \sum_{i=1}^m x_i = 1\}$ denote the standard $(m-1)$-simplex. A quadratic stochastic operator (QSO) $V : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ is a map of the form
\[
(V(x))_k = \sum_{i,j=1}^m p_{ij,k}\, x_i x_j, \qquad k = 1, \ldots, m,
\]
where the coefficients satisfy $p_{ij,k} = p_{ji,k} \geq 0$ and $\sum_{k=1}^m p_{ij,k} = 1$ for all $i, j$. The QSO $V$ is called Volterra if $p_{ij,k} = 0$ whenever $k \notin \{i, j\}$; equivalently, $(V(x))_k = x_k\bigl(1 + \sum_{i=1}^m a_{ki} x_i\bigr)$ for some skew-symmetric matrix $(a_{ki})$ with $|a_{ki}| \leq 1$.

Given a permutation $\tau$ of $\{1, \ldots, m\}$, define the permuted operator $V_\tau : S^{m-1} \to S^{m-1}$ by
\[
(V_\tau(x))_k = (V(x))_{\tau(k)}, \qquad k = 1, \ldots, m.
\]
When $\tau$ is not the identity, $V_\tau$ is in general a non-Volterra QSO.

For an arbitrary Volterra QSO $V$ and an arbitrary permutation $\tau$, describe the asymptotic behavior of the trajectories $\{V_\tau^n(x)\}_{n \geq 0}$ for $x \in S^{m-1}$: determine convergence/divergence, fixed and periodic points, $\omega$-limit sets, and any other long-term dynamical features.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains broadly open in full generality. Partial results have been established for specific subclasses: superpositions of Volterra and permuted Volterra QSOs on the two-dimensional simplex have been analyzed (trajectories shown to converge to periodic orbits or diverge), and certain classes of permuted Volterra QSOs in low dimensions have been investigated. However, the asymptotic behavior of permuted $\ell$-Volterra QSOs and the general case for arbitrary $m$ and arbitrary $\tau$ has not been resolved.

status_evidence.title: On a Superposition of Volterra and Permuted Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Trajectories either converge to a periodic trajectory or diverge; periodic and fixed points are described.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for superpositions involving permuted Volterra QSOs on the 2D simplex.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of quadratic operators generated by China's Five elements philosophy
status_evidence.snippet: Investigates dynamics of certain permuted Volterra-type QSOs.
status_evidence.claim: Specific subclasses of permuted Volterra QSOs have been studied, but a full general theory is not given.

status_evidence.title: On Dynamics of ℓ-Volterra Quadratic Stochastic Operators
status_evidence.snippet: Asymptotic behavior of permuted ℓ-Volterra QSOs has not been investigated yet.
status_evidence.claim: The general permuted Volterra asymptotic behavior problem remains open.
